title: Correlations between causal effect sizes of proximal SNPs vary with functional annotations and implicate stabilizing selection.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Figshare article 24716877 (CC BY 4.0) API listing: 8 files. Small ones opened: trait_list_paper.txt (70 traits, e.g. biochemistry_Albumin), annot_pair136.txt (136 lines, each a path to a SNP-pair annotation matrix in .npz format split by distance bin, LD (linkage disequilibrium, the correlation between nearby SNPs) sign and allele-frequency class), main.avgr (binary/opaque). Sizes seen: snp_info.zip 299 MB, annot_single165.zip 489 MB, annot_pair136.zip 2.08 GB, ldspec_results.zip 73 MB (not downloaded: over the 50 MB cap). Zenodo 20399367 is only a 329 KB MIT-licensed code release.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That ldspec_results.zip holds per-trait LDSPEC estimates; the 14,820,648-SNP count; the average N = 305,646 UK Biobank samples per trait. Full text was not retrievable (Europe PMC 500 error); used the abstract and the Figshare description.

a1_downloadable.note: Figshare files have public download URLs (checked via API, small files fetched). Individual UK Biobank genotypes are controlled access but aren't needed for the released summary-level files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No measured per-item outcome exists. The only candidate targets are trait-by-annotation effect-correlation estimates in ldspec_results.zip (paper description; file not opened). Any SNP-level target would have to be built by fitting a statistical model to GWAS (genome-wide association study) summary statistics.

a3_inputs_present.note: SNP annotations (165 single-SNP, 136 SNP-pair) are released as files; seen in the listing only, not opened.

a4_units_stated.note: Correlations are unitless; not a concern.

a5_enough_rows.note: The estimate table is about 70 traits x 136 annotations (from the file listing and the paper's description). The values aren't independent, and only 70 traits are truly distinct. Row count unverified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: >2.8 GB compressed annotations plus LD scores and GWAS summary statistics in separate Figshare articles
a6_fits_laptop.note: Rebuilding SNP-level inputs means the 2.08 GB pair-annotation zip plus LD scores across 14.8M SNPs. That's near or over the ~5 GB usable working-set limit, and the paper doesn't say how big things get once decompressed.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 70 traits in trait_list_paper.txt matches the abstract's 70 diseases/traits.

a8_label_provenance.note: Every candidate label is a regression estimate output by LDSPEC itself (a statistical model), computed from LD scores and annotations: the same quantities that would serve as features. That makes it both circular and leaky by construction.

existing_models.name: LDSPEC (this paper; LD SNP-pair effect correlation regression, a statistical estimator)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not a predictive model. Validated in simulations; reports estimates such as -0.37 ± 0.09 for low-frequency, positive-LD SNP pairs 0-100 bp apart.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Full discussion not retrieved; abstract points to stabilizing selection and linkage masking as the explanation.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Nucleotide Transformer (DNA models) could in principle embed SNP context
backbone.hardware: Would need embeddings for millions of SNPs; impractical on a CPU laptop

integration.partner_dataset: UK Biobank GWAS summary statistics (Price lab Figshare) or the AlphaGenome variant-effect atlas
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence-model variant-effect scores explain which SNP pairs have correlated effects? But there is no SNP-pair-level measured label to test this against.

controls.positive_control: Effect correlation decaying with distance (stated in the abstract)
controls.external_validation: None independent; TenK10K eQTL (expression quantitative trait locus) LDSPEC analysis on GitHub exists but also produces model estimates

honest_claim_h3: A model could only re-predict LDSPEC's own summary estimates from the same annotations used to compute them. That isn't a biological claim.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use functional annotations of nearby DNA variant pairs to predict how strongly their effects on disease are correlated.
plain_idea.train_on: Annotation categories for SNP (single-letter DNA variant) pairs, about 136 categories across 70 traits. The number of independent examples is unknown and small.
plain_idea.predict: The effect-size correlation between linked SNPs. The 'truth' is itself an estimate from the paper's statistical method, not a direct measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Statistical geneticists modelling heritability would care, but the paper's own estimator already answers the question, so a model adds little.

more_or_better_data.why: We'd use exactly the paper's own released annotations and estimates, no more.

confidence_score.why: LDSPEC already reports a standard error for each estimate (e.g. ±0.09).

models_beatable.why: LDSPEC (2026) is an estimator fitted to the data, not a predictor with a held-out test set, so there's nothing to beat.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No measured label exists that new data could improve predictions of; the target is the method's own output.

ml_idea: Predict SNP-pair effect correlations from functional annotations or DNA-model embeddings. Rejected: the only targets are LDSPEC's own estimates (70 traits x 136 annotations), computed from the same annotations.

effort.compute_note: Working set is the sum of the Figshare zip sizes seen in the listing; nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: the file listing shows no measured per-SNP or per-pair label, only per-trait estimates from the method.

verdict_reason: Statistical-genetics methods paper. Its released data is SNP annotations plus LDSPEC's own regression estimates for 70 traits x 136 annotation categories, so any label is model output computed from the would-be features (A8, A2), there are too few independent examples (A5), and rebuilding SNP-level inputs means multi-GB files (A6).
